title: Does the `meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"` tag allow lists of policies?

labels.name: security/privacy
labels.description: There are security or privacy implications

labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to write tests

body:
The [html spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html#attr-meta-http-equiv-content-security-policy) says that the `content` of an `` tag should be a [`serialized-policy`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#grammardef-serialized-policy) and should be parsed according to [Parse a serialized CSP](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#parse-serialized-policy). This implies that it does _not_ allow multiple comma-separated policies, such as `img-src 'none', script-src 'sha256-lLvWePLrgCn07EcwYB0JPy65n3OloEYiWK34Ql9Zdmc='`. That would be a [`serialized-csp-list`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#serialized-csp-list), parsed according to [Parse a serialized CSP list](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#parse-serialized-policy-list), which nothing I can find actually uses. (Also, that algorithm returns multiple policies, each of which would need to be enforced.) However, both Chrome and Safari _do_ allow policy lists such as the above. Firefox and the [Nu HTML checker](https://validator.w3.org/nu/) do not - Firefox attempts to parse it as a single policy including the `,`, while the Nu HTML checker considers it an outright error. As far as I can tell, the [web platform tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/tree/dff3a6865c67b469be3b9bc1f4b318554008931b/content-security-policy/meta) do not cover this case. [Here](https://bakkot.github.io/misc/csp-violation-demo.html) is a simple page with the above comma-separated CSP, which contains both an image and an inline script with no hash. Its source is below. Which is the intended behavior?
